newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil squeezed by falling futures and prems.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil squeezed by falling futures and prems.

text.p: There was no respite for NWE gas oil on Friday as falling futures and easier premiums squeezed outright prices lower.
March IPE gas oil closed $2.00 a tonne weaker at $162.50, in dull activity in line with lower U.S heating oil.

Barge premiums were also lower by $1.50 or so with Rotterdam refinery material done at March IPE -50 cents fob with bids heard by late afternoon down to March IPE -$1.00 and offers wavering around -25 cents. On Thursday the level was heard around flat to +$1 fob.
"Prompt gas oil is weak and buyers know that so pressurise as much as they can," said one trader. Storage material went at March IPE -$2.

Russian material had another busy day although premiums weakened. Two 40,000 tonne cargoes were done. One went at mean of means -75 cents for March 10-12 cif ARA while a more prompt cargo was able to secure only March IPE -50 cents cif ARA. Yesterday the market talked around March IPE flat.
Traders said they had seen one player picking up something like 160,000 tonnes of Russian this week.
"I'd like to take some myself and store it ahead of the contango," said one dealer.

FOD and DIN cargo activity was slow. FOD premiums were pegged notionally around flat, steady on Thursday, but interest was noticeably absent. Second half March, heard offered earlier at March IPE +$2-3 cif, was not attracting any serious business, traders said.
German buyers in particular look relatively full.
Diesel premiums were also weaker with offers heard around March IPE +$14 cif NWE, but no takers. A 20,000 tonnes German intermediate cargo was sold at March IPE +$10.50 cif Hamburg.

The additional Indian tender for diesel was awarded late on Friday amounting to three 45,000 tonne cargoes, according to initial trading sources. The volume was not thought high enough to make a significant impact.
